scenario: AITA for deleting my stepbrothers profile on my Nintendo switch? | At the beginning of the school year I had to watch my stepbrother for a week while my dad and his mom went on a trip to help out her parents with something. Brought my switch with me because my school is more than an hour away and I wanted something to do on the train during my commute everyday. My stepbrother wanted to play on it. Him being so into it actually turned into a big help to distract him while I studied, so I made a new profile on it for him so he wouldn’t mess up my saves. When I got back to school I eventually got annoyed with having to click on my profile each time I started a game and each time I went to the eshop. So I just deleted his profile. So, this early this morning I got on the train to go to my dads for thanksgiving. I usually go home to my moms, but she and my stepdad are going to see his family and Im not up for going plane trip. Anyway I brought my switch again for the train ride. Just a little while ago my stepbrother picked it up to start playing and came into the kitchen, where I was talking with my dad, freaking out because his Zelda save was gone and he wanted me to help him fix it. When I told him I deleted it he started crying. Like not full on crying, but his eyes were watery a little and red. Now he’s holed up in his room. My dad thinks it was mean of me to delete it because I know my stepbrother was enjoying playing it. I didn’t think it was a big deal since I usually never bring my switch over when I visit.

During that week, the stepbrother got really into playing, which actually helped him stay distracted while the person studied. So, the profile was useful for both of them. It kept the stepbrother entertained and allowed the person to focus on their studies without worrying about their games being messed up. After the week was over, the person went back to school. They found it annoying to switch profiles every time they wanted to play a game or go to the eShop. So, they decided to delete the stepbrother's profile. That seems like a minor inconvenience for them, but maybe they didn't consider how it would affect the stepbrother. Fast forward to Thanksgiving, the person brings the Switch again. The dad thinks it was mean, and the person is probably feeling some guilt or confusion about whether they did the right thing. So, why might deleting the profile be wrong? Well, the stepbrother had been using that profile for a week, and it was a way for him to enjoy the Switch. By deleting it, the person not only removed the profile but also any progress the stepbrother had made, like his Zelda save. That's a big deal because losing progress in a game can be really frustrating and upsetting, especially if the person didn't communicate their decision beforehand. The person might have thought it was just a profile and not a big deal, but to the stepbrother, it was his way of enjoying the game. The lack of communication is a key issue here. The person didn't tell the stepbrother they were going to delete the profile, so it came as a surprise, which made the situation worse. Additionally, the person didn't consider the emotional impact. That's why the dad thinks it was mean—it's about more than just the profile; it's about respecting the stepbrother's feelings and interests. On the other hand, the person might argue that the profile was on their own Switch, so they have the right to manage it as they see fit. However, since the stepbrother was using it with their permission, there's an expectation of respect for the time and effort the stepbrother put into his games. In conclusion, while the person had the right to manage their Switch, deleting the profile without communication and causing emotional distress makes it the wrong action. It's important to consider others' feelings, especially when sharing personal devices, and to communicate any changes that might affect them.
